newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand plans measures to curb short-term debt.
newsitem.headline: Thailand plans measures to curb short-term debt.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand said on Wednesday new measures were being considered to control rising short-term foreign debt which had led to a downgrade of the country's short-term rating by Moody's Investors Service.

"The bank accepts Moody's views on Thailand's short-term foreign debt problem. We are monitoring it and considering new measures to solve the problem," said central bank governor Rergnchai Marakanond.
He did not give details of the planned measures.
Moody's said Thailand's downgrade reflected its increased vulnerability to a financial shock through the balance of payments after recent rapid accumulation of its short-term external debt.

According to central bank data, Thailand's short-term foreign debt rose to $41.1 billion at end-1995 from $15.4 billion at end-1991. The end-1995 figure represented about half of the country's total external debt.
The Bank of Thailand, however, said on Tuesday that its recent restrictive measures aimed at curbing short-term capital inflow had been effective.
It said the proportion of short-term loans in Thailand's total fresh borrowing declined to 47.5 percent in July from about 84 percent in late 1995 and early 1996.
